# Quick Add and Inbox native integration verification

2026-10-25. Implemented and installed in ordinary Work. No commit, push, pull, migration, task restoration or collaborator deployment was performed.

## Product behavior

Compact Quick Add retains its header, input, file capture and immediate Send to Inbox. Capture does not wait for native admission. More options retains Task/Note; native Task embeds the existing `mountLiveTaskForm`, importance/date/description/Step controls and native location picker. Enter uses that editor's existing form submission. Global creation requires a visible Project/Resource choice. Physical source context preselects the owning workspace and an unambiguous folder; root is valid.

Inbox retains two columns, All/Texts/Files, timestamps, sorting, selection and scrolling. The selected thought is fully editable, with Create task, New note and Add to existing note. Workspace is visible; native details are optional. Specification bars, completeness sorts and missing-detail labels are absent. Old completeness preferences are displayed as newest-first without rewriting them on open. Per-action drafts preserve recorded choices; saved items are not migrated on load.

New notes, attachment staging/moves and exact note insertion retain the existing Markdown/file service and input/hash/rollback checks. Native mode also allows explicit workspace-root note/file destinations and existing root notes. Legacy-only service behavior and its frozen assertions remain intact.

## Native operation and recovery boundary

Task creation uses the existing production owner runtime, application adapter, native writer and host-owned REQUEST-RETENTION evidence. An Inbox item's existing operation field links the original operation ID, owner, exact input and intended values; it is not an outcome ledger. Allocated task/Step IDs and compiled commands remain in native retention. A matching validated receipt confirms cleanup after an interrupted acknowledgement; retries do not allocate another task. Missing/conflicting/unverifiable outcomes preserve the capture and require existing recovery. Direct Add retains one attempt identity and creates no Inbox item.

Git admission freezes all six authoritative reservation domains, including Inbox. Capturing/organizing changes that observation. The production host now offers a bounded same-authority drain/reopen with fresh validated inventory before first native admission, and background refresh when capture closes/cleanup finishes. It verifies retained outcomes, preserves every original command/guard/receipt, releases the old lease, and reopens the same config/authority through the existing admission path. Concurrent callers recheck after an in-flight refresh. Existing panel/History subscriptions rebind. Conversion refreshes only its target owner; a failed unrelated shared owner does not block a healthy private/Resource target. No core policy, persistence, receipt, recovery or N4 protocol was changed.

Existing scripts contain additional assertions; 58 is the runner entry count.
- New cases cover full multiline text, optional properties/Steps, global destination, physical Resource ownership, folder location, failed cleanup, lost UI acknowledgement, reconstruction before native preparation, exact retry, initialization-independent capture, unsupported inputs and an initially checked null-time Step without duplicate events.
- Two relevant declaration runners: zero diagnostics (TypeScript 6.0.3).
- Genuine isolated Obsidian: 21 shared-Project checks and 13 private/Resource multi-owner checks. Capture cases use the actual plugin service and shared UI source. Verified native direct creation (including trusted Electron Enter input), Inbox conversion, old typed drafts, file capture/moves, root-note creation, append/position validation, cleanup interruption, pre-existing consumer reconnection, native publication, History/Statistics, restart and lease draining. Destructive writes were confined to guarded synthetic vaults.
- Hidden multi-owner exit emitted an Electron callback-after-window-close diagnostic; its exit status passed and quit evidence has zero remaining locks. Ordinary Work shutdown also released all eleven locks without intervention.

## Ordinary Work verification and preservation

Installed plugin startup and real process restart admitted all eleven existing authorities. Authoritative before/after models match exactly: **67 tasks, 17 Steps, 18 Inbox items and 182 Legacy History records**. The original Pulsed Optomechanics task remains intact. Every owner's native History evidence also matches. No real task, completion, note, file or Inbox entry was created/modified as a smoke test.

Used actual installed Quick Add/Inbox controls to check compact capture readiness, explicit global destination, eleven choices, embedded native editor/location/keyboard form, cancellation, full Inbox content/actions, filters and selection. Opened the original task editor without saving and verified existing Statistics (182 inputs). Actual Work capture operations were draft-only; destination writes were tested in disposable Obsidian. The desktop automation helper was unavailable, so installed checks used the genuine application's controls/API rather than OS pointer automation.

Normal graceful shutdown released all eleven writer locks. Restart preserved the exact task/Step identities and data. Work is left open, responsive, on Home with eleven leases owned by its live renderer. Temporary debugging is off.

All 178 repository/retention/recovery files compare byte-for-byte with the initial baseline (excluding ephemeral leases). Full local application data and shared application-data models also match; all six protected domains match. Markdown retirement, archives, shared bindings/genesis, Git transport state and existing native authority identities were not changed. Git HEAD and every staged path/mode/object/stage entry match the initial baseline. Index cache bytes changed; `index-final.json` verifies all entries against the preserved original index. No index restoration was performed; source work remains uncommitted.

## Remaining boundaries

Native attachments remain unavailable; file captures use existing note/file organization. Phase/recurrence/nested task operations remain guarded. A saved Phase is explicitly surfaced and must be left unassigned before native conversion. Uncertain old Legacy task operations are not silently redirected; uncertain native operations use the existing operator recovery interface. A reservation change may briefly put shared consumers into loading during validated readmission. No real-capture conversion was performed simply for testing.
